sections.h2: Who sends and who collects the property tax bill in Jackson County, MO?
sections.html:
Two county departments split the work. The Assessment Department values every parcel, and the Department of Collection mails the bills and takes payment. If your question is about what the house is worth on paper, call Assessment at 816-881-1330. If it is about what you owe or how to pay, call Collection at 816-881-3232.

Assessment keeps real property customer service at 1300 Washington St. in Kansas City, and individual personal property at the Historic Truman Courthouse, 112 W. Lexington in Independence. Both counters open at 8 a.m. and close at 5 p.m. on weekdays, and holidays the county observes are closed. Collection also works from both courthouses and answers email at Collections@jacksongov.org.

A seller in Jackson County, Missouri should pull the parcel record from the county's public property access portal before listing. It shows the assessed figures that the bill is built from.

sections.h2: What does Jackson County cover, and who lives here?
sections.html:
Jackson County sits on the Kansas border in western Missouri and has two county seats, Independence and Kansas City. It was organized on December 15, 1826, and the Missouri River forms most of its northern edge. Neighbors include Clay, Cass and Lafayette counties in Missouri and Johnson and Wyandotte counties in Kansas.

The county counts 19 communities, among them Blue Springs, Grandview, Lee's Summit, Raytown, Oak Grove, Grain Valley and Sugar Creek. All of them share one assessment and collection system, with each taxing district adding its own levy line to the statement.

  • Land area: 604.52 square miles
  • Residents counted in the 2025 Census estimate: 732,994, up 2.2% from the 2020 base
  • Homes and apartments: 344,038 units
  • Share of households that own: 59.1%
  • Middle price tag on an owned home: $230,500

Median household income across the 2020 to 2024 survey years is $68,577, and typical gross rent is $1,197. Those who carry a mortgage report a median of $1,639 a month in owner costs, taxes included.

sections.h2: When is the Jackson County property tax bill due?
sections.html:
The bill is due on December 31. The county mails bills during November, and for 2025 the mailing was expected to finish by December 12. If nothing has arrived by about December 8, call the Collector, because an unreceived bill still carries the same deadline.

A mailed check counts only if the USPS stamps it by year end, and the county suggests mailing several days ahead because drop-box mail does not always get a same-day postmark. Checks go to the Jackson County Collector with the property account number written on them. Online payment through payments.jacksongov.org stops at 11:40 p.m. on December 31, and the two courthouse drop boxes lock at midnight that night. Cash should never go in a drop box.

Fees for paying online are a $2.00 transaction charge, plus $1.25 for an e-check or 2.75% for a debit or credit card. Paying in person or by check avoids those add-ons.

sections.h2: What is the process to contest a Jackson County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the Board of Equalization, an independent panel of county taxpayers that now sits only at 1300 Washington in Kansas City. The 2026 application window ran until July 13, 2026, so that deadline has passed. Watch the board's page for the 2027 window.

Evidence that carries weight includes a certified appraiser's report, a sales contract with the settlement statement for a recent purchase, and written repair estimates. The board will not look at evidence shown on a phone or tablet at the hearing, and it does not make copies for you.

  • If you signed a stipulated value offered by Assessment, your board appeal is cancelled and you can no longer go to the State Tax Commission.
  • If you skip the stipulation, you keep the hearing, and a loss there can be taken to the State Tax Commission.
  • Commercial appeals to the Commission require a lawyer.
  • Withdrawing an appeal must be in writing from the homeowner and can be done any time.

sections.h2: Must the full bill be paid while a Jackson County appeal is open?
sections.html:
Yes. The county tells owners to pay the printed amount before year end, even when a hearing is still ahead. Recalculations for 2026 appeal decisions are suspended until January 2027, and when a lower value is set, the excess is refunded automatically.

Paying under protest is optional. Missouri statute 139.031 asks for full payment before the delinquency date plus a written statement of the grounds and the value you claim. The county notes that a protest can slow a refund, since protested money is released only on a set schedule, and that protesting does not protect or harm your right to appeal. Partial payments are taken for real property, but interest, penalties and fees accrue on whatever remains unpaid after December 31, and partial payments cannot be made online.

sections.h2: Is there a cap or credit on residential assessments in Jackson County?
sections.html:
The county announced a 15% assessment cap for qualifying residential homeowners, tied to a review of the 2023 single-family assessments. Per the county's FAQ sheet updated December 8, 2025, relief comes as a credit on the 2026, 2027 and 2028 bills, spread evenly across those three years. No application is needed, no refund checks go out, and the 2025 bill still had to be paid in full.

The county says the tax money had already been distributed to schools, fire districts, libraries and cities, which is why it is a credit and not a check. The relief covers residential real estate only, and vehicles and boats are not part of it. Call Assessment if your bill looks wrong rather than assuming a credit has posted.

sections.h2: Which senior programs exist for Jackson County homeowners?
sections.html:
Two county programs apply to residential property, and an eligible owner may use both. The Senior Property Tax Credit offsets future increases. The Senior Citizen Quad Payment Program lets the owner spread the county bill over four equal installments with no interest or penalties.

  • Both require age 62 or older by December 31 of the relevant year and the home as the only primary residence.
  • The Quad program also requires prior-year taxes to be current, a home assessed solely as residential, and ownership by the person, not a trust.
  • Taxes paid from a mortgage escrow are not eligible for the Quad program.
  • The credit covers ad valorem principal only. Special assessments and CID or TDD charges are due in full.

The state Circuit Breaker credit is a separate program run by the Missouri Department of Revenue at 573-751-3505.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax after a Jackson County house changes hands?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate tax attaches to the parcel itself, so the incoming owner answers for any balance. The county explains that the year's tax is usually split between the two parties, with the buyer credited for the days the seller held title. Normally no money goes to the Collector at the sale itself, though a closing company may pay any amount that is currently due.

Tell the Assessment office the new owner and mailing address, because a bill can otherwise go to the seller's old address. When a lender pays from escrow, send the bill on to the lender. Ask the closing company which tax year it is prorating.

faqs.q: When does Jackson County, MO stop accepting on-time property tax payments?
faqs.a: At the end of December 31. A mailed check must be postmarked by then, and the online system cuts off at 11:40 p.m. Interest, penalties and fees start accruing the next day.

faqs.q: Is it too late to contest my 2026 Jackson County value?
faqs.a: Yes. The 2026 filing window at the Board of Equalization ended July 13, 2026. Look for the 2027 window on the board's page, and pay the 2026 bill in full by December 31 meanwhile.

faqs.q: Does a refund after a value cut require a protest payment?
faqs.a: No. A lower value triggers an automatic refund, and a protest can slow it down. A protest payment must be on time, in full and accompanied by a written statement.

faqs.q: How is the tax split when a Jackson County home sells midyear?
faqs.a: The buyer owes the full bill by December 31, while the seller's share usually appears as a credit to the buyer at closing. Ask the closing company how your contract divides it.

faqs.q: What address do I use to mail a Jackson County tax payment?
faqs.a: Make it payable to the Jackson County Collector with the property account number on it. Protest payments go to Attention: Protest, P.O. Box 219747, Kansas City, MO 64121-9747. Call 816-881-3232 for the current regular mailing address.
